jobs.title: AI Red Team Engineer
jobs.description: **About Hamming** ----------------- Hamming is the security layer for voice and chat agents. Banks, health systems, and other enterprises are putting agents on phone lines where anyone can reach them, and where the agent can verify identity, read an account, and act. We attack those agents before criminals do, with the owner's permission, show what they fall for, and keep every fix tested on every release. We are one of the fastest engineering teams in the world. We prod deploy 4x / day. Devin Case Study Ranked \#1 Eng team OpenAI Dev Day 100billion token list **The role** ------------ Our researchers find the failure by hand. You make it happen a thousand times, against authorized targets, with evidence a customer can inspect, and again on every release. You own the harness: the runner that places calls and chat sessions, the evaluators that decide what a result means, and the replay that shows what changed. Thousands of concurrent calls, bounded, cancellable, observable. **What you'll do** ------------------ * **Build the attack harness.** A new technique is a new definition, not a new system. * **Generate useful variations.** Branch multi\-turn scenarios and voice conditions with the objective and conditions explicit. * **Make results trustworthy.** A successful attack, a refusal, an infrastructure failure, and an inconclusive result are distinguishable and inspectable. * **Make findings reproducible.** Scenario, configuration, model versions, tool events, outcomes, replay, and comparison. * **Keep fixes fixed.** Validated findings become regression tests that run on every change, with noise controlled. **What you'll bring** --------------------- * 3\+ years building backend services, async workers, or test infrastructure in Python or TypeScript, with the failure cases and the tests. * An adversarial mind: offensive tooling, CTFs, fuzzing, or a security project. The title does not matter. * Judgment about evidence: when an automated evaluator is enough and when a human has to look. * Idempotency, backpressure, observability, and limits that are enforced rather than documented. **Nice to have** ---------------- * Agent frameworks, voice or telephony systems, or LLM evaluation infrastructure * A security finding of your own, responsibly disclosed **How we work** --------------- We start with the customer problem, ship daily, and let evidence decide what comes next. Use AI tools to move faster and own the result. Direct, low ego, serious work. **Benefits and perks** ---------------------- * Competitive salary and meaningful equity * Health, dental, and vision coverage * Every frontier AI tool, fully paid, from day one * Conferences and events we sponsor * Flexible PTO * Offices in San Francisco and Austin; remote in the United States for most roles

jobs.title: AI Solutions Engineer
jobs.description: **About Health Data Innovations** --------------------------------- Founded in 2010, Health Data Innovations (HDI) allows providers and payers to seamlessly integrate external administrative data into their internal systems. HDI’s tech\-enabled data management system and processes codify decades of knowledge to ingest, cleanse, standardize, and validate payer claims and administrative data. The system reflects HDI’s extensive experience with data from a broad spectrum of payers and vendors. By outsourcing data acquisition and integration to HDI, clients can spend more time working with the data and less time on data integration issues. In 2023, Hughes \& Company invested in HDI to build on the company’s success enabling healthcare providers in value\-based care arrangements. HDI provides clients with mission\-critical data that is necessary for contractual obligations and underpins programs of substantial value. As risk\-based arrangements proliferate and increase in complexity, HDI’s differentiated technology is a critical tool to enable the success of these programs. **The Role** ------------ We're looking for an AI Solutions Engineer to build and run the AI tools, integrations, and workflows that put AI to work across HD Innovations, and to lead our move to agentic AI. Our AI initiative is already live: enterprise AI assistants and coding tools, a private model gateway on Amazon Bedrock, custom connectors to our business systems, and local models running on our own GPU hardware. Our next step is AI agents that take action across our systems, and we want to get there quickly. This is a hands\-on role on a small team. Most of your time goes to building AI solutions and agents; the rest goes to the infrastructure they run on, including cloud services, identity, servers, and GPU hosts, all in a security\-first, HITRUST\-governed environment. **Why This Role** ----------------- * Build AI that does real work across the whole business, not just one department * Work directly with executives and every function at HDI to find where AI can make the biggest difference * Shape how HDI adopts AI — your ideas influence the roadmap * Build agents that handle complex work in a high\-stakes, regulated healthcare environment **What You'll Do** ------------------ * Work with business users to find processes where AI can help, and decide the right approach: an assistant, an AI\-assisted workflow, or an agent * Build and improve AI\-assisted workflows, skills, and plugins that put AI into everyday processes * Lead the move to agentic AI: design, build, and deploy agents and multi\-step workflows using tool use / function calling, prompt and context design, and agent frameworks * Build and support Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, database bridges, and Microsoft 365 integrations so AI tools and agents can safely reach the data and systems they need * Test and evaluate AI output for accuracy and reliability, and catch regressions before they reach users * Build in guardrails, least\-privilege permissions, human\-in\-the\-loop approvals, and audit logging, especially where AI touches sensitive healthcare data * Own AI solutions in production: monitor behavior, usage, and cost; jobs.title: Automation Engineer
jobs.description: If you thrive in fast paced environments, enjoy hands\-on problem solving, and want to make a measurable impact while working with modern automation and control systems, this role offers the challenge, autonomy, and growth opportunities to take your engineering career to the next level. In this role, you won’t just maintain systems—you’ll continuously improve them. You’ll apply your controls and automation knowledge to optimize preventive maintenance strategies, diagnose sophisticated issues, and enhance the performance of industry leading technologies such as conveyors, sortation systems, PLCs, scanners, vision systems, print ‑and ‑apply equipment, and SCADA platforms. Your work will directly influence uptime, safety, and operational excellence across mission critical facilities. \*This is a day shift opportunity\-8:00 AM\-4:30 PM CST\+On call on weekends\* What You’ll Do * Promote a safe working environment by complying with all applicable codes, regulations, governmental agencies, and company directives related to system operations and work safety. * Troubleshoot and modify software programs for material handling control systems, including PLC/PC controllers, Allen Bradley Controllogix/Compactlogix PLC platform and RSLogix 5000 software package. * Act as first level escalation in troubleshooting support, both on\-site and remotely, as well as during and after business hours, to repair all MHE controls software systems. Respond quickly to emergency situations, summoning assistance as needed. * Inspect systems to ensure the operation of equipment is within design capabilities and achieve operational conditions prescribed by the client. * Oversee scope of development, work request initiation, scheduling, and inspection of work performed by outside contractors, which includes proprietary work, licensed installations, upgrades, and maintenance and inspection of specialized systems. * Engineer process solutions and reliability improvement from concept to network implementation. * Monitor Industrial networks such as Ethernet, ControlNet, DeviceNet, Profibus, AS\-I, motor control systems, servo drives, frequency drives, and electrical distribution systems. * Monitor material handling equipment metrics and partner with site team to resolve equipment electrical problems that create performance deficiencies. * Proactively and effectively communicate with multiple stakeholders including, but not limited to, leadership, operations and the maintenance team on technical issues and project timelines and production impacts. * Facilitate analysis and reviews of failures and processes to provide recommendations to implement improvements or retraining to avoid future incidents. * Perform controls systems assessments to maintain and improve equipment reliability. * Clearly communicate technical issues, project timelines, and product impacts with site leadership, operations and maintenance teams. * Cultivate positive working relationships with our Client and the Operations Maintenance team members. * Perform other job\-related duties as needed or assigned. What You’ll Need * Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future. * Bachelor's Degree preferred with 2\-5 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education may be considered. * Experience in at least two engineering design cycles including specification, component selection and programming. * 2\+ years of experience working with PLC programming, robotics system components and controls, and SCADA\-based monitoring and control systems. * Ability to be available and work in a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays. * Ability to independently solve problems and carry out general instructions in standard situations with limited to no oversight. * Meet the physical requirements of this role including stooping, standing, walking, climbing stairs/ladders, and the ability to lift/carry heavy loads of 50 lbs. or more. * Ability to guide the exchange of sensitive, complicated, and difficult information, convey performance expectations, and handle problems. Preferred Qualifications * 2\+ years apprenticeship or equivalent experience in Control Systems troubleshooting/ programming. * Experience supporting a range of different conveyors and sortation systems. * Experience with robotic maintenance. * In\-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products. Examples include Word, Excel, Outlook, etc. * Extensive organizational skills with a strong inquisitive mindset. * Advanced math skills. Ability to calculate difficult figures such as percentages, fractions, and other financial\-related calculations. You should be proficient in: * PLC Programming Experience * SCADA Experience

jobs.title: Due Diligence Engineer
jobs.description: **About Ornn** -------------- Ornn is building the financial infrastructure for AI compute. Our price indices are live on Bloomberg Terminal. We structure and trade compute hedging instruments. And we're now building a platform that brings exchange\-grade mechanics like order management, matching, scheduling, and settlement to how compute capacity gets reserved and allocated. We're a lean team in New York, backed by leading venture and strategic investors. ### **About the Role** Today the technical review of a new operator gets split across people who already have other jobs, which makes it both a bottleneck on bringing supply onto the platform and the place a lot of our risk quietly sits. You would own that review. When our supply team brings in a new operator, you are the person who reads the documentation and says whether the site is what it claims to be: racks and elevations, topology, power and cooling, heat exchangers, chassis, fiber and the network path. Then you run the process from there, chasing the gaps and driving to a yes or no rather than handing a list of questions to someone else. You'll work alongside the supply team, who bring the operator in, and finance, who run the commercial side of the same review. The technical judgment is yours. ### **What You'll Do** * Run the technical and IT review of every new supplier site: racks, topology, power and cooling, heat exchangers, chassis, cabling and network path. * Read operator documentation critically and find what is missing, not just what is there. * Project manage diligence end to end, chasing operators for the documents and answers you need and closing to a decision. * Set the standard for what an operator has to produce to get listed on Ornn, and tighten it as we learn. * Flag where a site's real capability does not match the service levels we are about to promise a customer. * Work with the supply team on new operators and with finance on commercial and financial diligence. * Stay close to capacity after it is signed, because what you find in diligence is what deployment and fleet operations inherit. **Requirements** * Hands\-on experience with data center infrastructure: power, cooling, racks, structured cabling and network topology. * Able to read site documentation, single line diagrams, rack elevations and network diagrams and tell whether they hold up. * Comfortable running a process, not only doing the review: owning the timeline, chasing people, closing items out. * Clear, direct writing. Your review has to be something a commercial team can act on. **Nice\-to\-Haves** * Time at a neocloud, colocation provider, data center developer or hyperscaler, doing site reviews, commissioning or deployments. * A mechanical or electrical engineering background, or deep enterprise IT infrastructure experience. * Familiarity with GPU cluster builds, InfiniBand fabrics and liquid cooling. * Vendor or site due diligence in a commercial setting, where the output was a decision rather than a report. * Exposure to infrastructure or private equity diligence processes. ### **Why This Role Matters** Ornn promises customers availability on capacity it does not own. That promise is made at diligence, not at deployment. Every service credit we pay, every late deployment and every penalty traces back to something a site review either caught or missed. This role is the gate, and today the gate is a few people doing it between other jobs. ### **Compensation and Benefits** Benefits include competitive salary, meaningful equity, health coverage, free meals, and additional benefits. This is a senior role with significant impact and equity upside. ### **Equal Opportunity Statement** Ornn is committed to building a diverse team. We evaluate candidates based on their ability to do the work, not on pedigree or background. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences. Compensation Range: $180K \- $250K

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description: **Company** ----------- Pramaana Labs is a frontier AI lab building the verification layer for AI. We turn complex human knowledge, including tax codes, legal rules, clinical guidelines and security protocols, into formal representations that support reasoning people can inspect and check. Our architecture pairs models trained to formalize and reason with a symbolic world model encoded in Lean 4\. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Palo Alto, Pramaana brings together researchers and formal methods experts from Google, DeepMind, and Glean. **The Role** ------------ The hardest questions in AI emerge when systems meet messy reality. Can ambiguous, exception\-filled rules be formalized faithfully? Can we distinguish what is proved from what is assumed, and make the results reliable enough to use? As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work where applied research, software engineering and customer problems meet. Alongside Pramaana engineers and researchers, you'll prototype and evaluate verifiable AI workflows, build tools and integrations, and help take promising systems into production. You'll investigate failures and turn lessons from the field into improvements to our research, models and core technology. We're looking for engineers who think from first principles, learn fast and care deeply about making AI reasoning verifiable. You don't need years of enterprise deployment experience. You'll have strong technical guidance while owning your work and handling real customer challenges with maturity. **What You'll Do** ------------------ * Understand the real technical problem. Work with customers and domain experts to turn source material, rules, exceptions and constraints into clear requirements and success criteria. * Prototype verifiable AI workflows. Experiment with model\-based formalization, symbolic reasoning and proof checking on challenging real\-world inputs. Find out what works and where it breaks. * Build rigorous evaluations. Create representative examples, edge cases and benchmarks to measure rule fidelity, correctness, coverage and robustness. Reproduce failures and investigate them carefully. * Take systems into production. Build and debug applications, APIs, tools and integrations. Iterate with customer teams, explain limitations and help deliver reliable workflows. * Close the loop with research. Work with researchers to turn customer issues and evaluation results into better representations, models, proof workflows and core technology. * Own problems and improve what comes next. Ask sharp questions, take responsibility for scoped work, communicate blockers early and turn one\-off fixes into reusable patterns where possible. **You Will Thrive in This Role If You Have** -------------------------------------------- * Strong software engineering fundamentals. You can write clean code, reason about data structures and algorithms, and debug unfamiliar problems. * First\-principles and logical thinking. You question assumptions, isolate the essential problem and explain your reasoning clearly. * High initiative and a habit of learning quickly. You have examples of making meaningful progress without waiting for detailed instructions. * A genuine interest in Pramaana's mission. You are deeply excited about reliable, verifiable AI to study the problem and build in this space. * Clear written and verbal communication, including the maturity to stay calm, be candid about uncertainty and work constructively with customers. * Comfort learning from more experienced engineers, asking for help when needed and incorporating feedback quickly. **Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have** ---------------------------------------------- * Built an impressive personal project, research prototype, hackathon project or meaningful open\-source contribution from scratch. * Experience with Python or TypeScript, APIs, backend development, LLM applications, evaluation or developer tools. * Explored formal verification, theorem proving, Lean, logic, symbolic reasoning or AI reliability through work or self\-directed learning. * Hands\-on experience working with users, handling unexpected problems or explaining technical ideas to non\-specialists.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description: ### **Who are we?** Newcode helps legal organizations build, govern, and deploy AI workflows connected to their knowledge and existing systems. Our Aurora workflow platform enables teams to turn firm expertise into repeatable workflows that operate within the firm’s technology environment. ### **The role** You'll own the backend behind our AI features. That's the APIs, the data pipelines, and the orchestration sitting between our product and the language models doing the work. In practice it means running retrieval over large sets of documents, getting dependable results out of LLMs and their tool calls, streaming responses to the UI, and processing long jobs in the background without things falling over. It isn't CRUD work. The hard parts here are keeping AI systems accurate and fast with confidential data, at production scale. You'll make architecture calls early and live with them. **Requirements** **Turn how legal work gets done into AI workflows lawyers trust** Newcode helps legal organizations build, govern, and deploy AI workflows connected to their knowledge and existing systems. Our Aurora workflow platform enables teams to turn firm expertise into repeatable workflows that operate within the firm's technology environment. Our clients are law firms and professional\-services teams. They know exactly where their work is slow, repetitive, or risky. What they don't know is how to turn that into an AI workflow they can trust with real client work. We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to do exactly that. This role reports to the Head of Forward Deployed Engineering. ### **The Opportunity** You'll work directly with clients to understand how their work actually gets done, and then build it in Aurora, our visual AI workflow builder. Aurora is low\-code. You design flows by connecting components on a canvas, configure the models, prompts, document search, and integrations, and write a short script where the canvas stops. The hard part isn't the code. It's understanding a messy process well enough to break it into steps a model can do reliably, seeing where it will fail before it does, and showing a skeptical partner at a law firm that it works. This role rewards judgment and engineering discipline more than seniority. We care more about how you think than how many years you've written code. You need to be comfortable with hands\-on technical work. For example, you can read API documentation to connect two systems, edit JSON files, write a short Python function when the canvas is not enough, and find out why a flow stopped working. ### **How the team works** You'll report to the Head of Forward Deployed Engineering, who manages the FDEs across our client pods and owns engineering quality, staffing, coaching, and technical delivery practices. What you will own * Sit with clients alongside the senior legal engineer and map how a piece of work gets done today: the inputs, the decisions, the exceptions, and who signs off. * Turn the workflow requirements into working flows in Aurora, such as document intake, clause extraction, contract review, drafting, and multi\-step agents. * Configure the building blocks: prompts, model choice, search over client documents, and connections to the systems clients already use, within each firm's access controls and confidentiality boundaries. * Write python scripts where configuration isn't enough, such as a custom component, a data transformation, or an API call, and flag the ones worth reusing across clients. * Test every flow against real examples and the evals agreed with the firm, find where it fails, and fix it before a client finds it. Show with evidence against the legal acceptance criteria, not a demo, that it works. * Run workshops and pilots, help deliver the AI Academy for each firm's Aurora users, and stay responsible for the flow after it goes live, with a named owner and support plan agreed before release. * Follow the FDE team's delivery playbook and technical standards, including design and code reviews, testing, traceability, monitoring, and human review suited to each flow's intended use. * Give realistic estimates, and raise scope changes, risks, and dependencies early with the senior legal engineer and the Head of Forward Deployed Engineering. * Bring what you learn back, through the Head of Forward Deployed Engineering, to Product and Engineering as patterns rather than anecdotes: missing features in Aurora, recurring requests and how often they come up, and bugs. * Help the team track delivery time, effort, workflow adoption, and component reuse, so that estimates and client outcomes improve over time. ### **What you bring** * You think in structure. Give you a vague process and you break it into clear steps, inputs, and decisions, and you see where it will go wrong. * You learn a new domain fast. You don't need a law degree, but you'll want to understand how a lawyer reviews a contract or runs a due diligence. * You explain things clearly to a law their needs, and help them realize the immense value AI can create. As part of our collaborative, high\-growth team, you'll work side by side with visionary founders at the forefront of AI and legal innovation, shaping both our product and the definition of AI native legal work. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work directly with clients on AI that ends up in real legal work, not in a demo. You'll help shape how we deploy Aurora, contributing to the Aurora playbook and the field patterns that make it into the product, and you'll grow with regular coaching from the Head of Forward Deployed Engineering, clear technical standards, and a team that delivers repeatably rather than through individual heroics. We believe in being transparent about what it's like to work at Newcode.ai. As a fast\-growing startup, we're building and evolving every day. That means not every process, playbook, or framework is already in place, and priorities can shift quickly. The people who thrive here are comfortable with ambiguity, take ownership, and don't wait for perfect direction. They are resourceful, proactive, and able to "figure it out", solving problems, creating structure where needed, and helping build the company as they go. If you are good with this, great! Keep reading to learn more. **Company stage.** Newcode is a growth\-stage legal AI company founded in 2021\. It has moved beyond early product validation into scaling deployments and expanding in the U.S. The company describes its product as a configurable AI platform that connects a firm's data, systems, and workflows, with controls for permissions, models, and deployment. **Funding.** Newcode has a total funding of $20 million. The Series A was led by OnDean Forward, with participation from The LegalTech Fund, Antiportfolio Ventures, Relativity's investment arm Rel Labs, and existing investors. **Traction and deployments.** Today Newcode serves more than 100 law firms and government agencies in Europe and the United States, with annual recurring revenue more than tripling over the prior 12 months. Check out our webpage for our most recent customers. **Why now is a compelling time to join.** Newcode is at an exciting stage of growth. With fresh Series A funding and strong customer and revenue growth, we are investing in the next chapter of our growth in Europe and the U.S. Our platform is moving beyond standalone AI tools and into the everyday workflows of leading legal teams. From firmwide deployments to integrated legal research, we are helping customers put AI to work on meaningful, real\-world challenges. As we expand our product, customer support, go\-to\-market, and partnerships, you will have the opportunity to take on important work and help shape how we grow. You will join a global team of more than 60 people, with the scale to serve major organizations and the agility to make a visible impact. If you are excited to build practical AI for the legal industry and help shape a company's next stage of growth, this is a great time to join Newcode. **Benefits** We offer competitive salary, **equity**, and bonus across all locations. Benefits are tailored to each country to meet local requirements and market practice: * **US (Chicago):** Medical, dental, and vision; 401(k); paid time off; * **Norway (Oslo) and Poland (Wrocław):** Statutory benefits plus local offerings, including pension, paid leave, and parental leave ### **The hiring process** * Stage 1: Screening call (15 minutes) * Stage 2: Case assessment: design and build a flow for a realistic client problem (1 hours) * Stage 3: Presentation of your case to the team, including the Head of Forward Deployed Engineering (3 hours) * Stage 4: CEO interview (15 minutes) Newcode is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants of all backgrounds. **Visa Sponsorship:** At this time, Newcode is unable to provide visa sponsorship. jobs.description: **About Us** ------------ Dashly is a fraud intelligence startup that uses data across employers, insurers, and contractors to fight fraud in injury claims. We expose fraud networks that cost Americans billions of dollars annually, slow commercial development, and erode trust in blue\-collar industries. Backed by Mosaic GP, Altai Ventures, and Remarkable Ventures, with a $5\.8M seed round. **About the Role** ------------------ Fraud is rarely one person acting alone. Organized claim fraud is often run by networks: groups of associated people acting together through a pattern of related claims over time. The cost falls on carriers, contractors, and the industries that depend on fair claims. The evidence is public but fragmented across dockets, deposition transcripts, claim files, and social media. Dashly investigates organized fraud enterprises: formal or informal groups of individuals, and the counsel, providers, and associates around them, linked by shared addresses, phone numbers, employers, and narratives. We build cases around the structure of organized fraud: the enterprise, each member's association with it, a pattern of related conduct, how long that conduct continues, and its reach across state lines. Our work gives clients and their counsel evidence for fraud litigation. As a Fraud Intelligence Analyst, you will design, run, and QA the automated OSINT workflows behind our investigations. You will build and orchestrate agentic AI workflows (LLM agents) for account discovery and attribution, court\-filing and deposition extraction, media review, and report drafting. You will integrate third\-party OSINT, licensed, and public\-records data sources via API, and you will own detection quality (precision, recall, and false\-positive rate) across the pipeline. This role suits a recent graduate in cybercrime, cybersecurity, criminal justice, intelligence, computer science, or a related field who combines a builder's mindset with an investigator's rigor. Prior military or government experience is welcome. **What You'll Do** ------------------ * Design and operationalize automated OSINT workflows that take a claim from initial identifiers to a finished report: account discovery, attribution, collection, court\-document extraction, and link analysis. * Build, prompt, and supervise AI agents and LLM\-based automation for investigative tasks, with human\-in\-the\-loop verification before any output reaches a client. * Integrate OSINT, licensed, and public\-records data sources through their APIs, and evaluate each new data source on historical cases before production use. * Measure and improve detection quality: track precision, recall, and false\-positive and false\-negative rates against analyst\-confirmed accounts, and tune workflows accordingly. * Identify, attribute, and verify claimants' online accounts and records using strong identifiers (address, phone, email, date of birth). * Review public photos and posts and flag activity that contradicts claimant testimony or statements to the insurer. * Extract facts from court filings, deposition transcripts, and claim files, and use link analysis to map relationships among claimants, counsel, addresses, phone numbers, and associates, documenting enterprise structure, member associations, and patterns of related conduct across claims. * Produce clear, evidence\-backed investigative reports that clients and their counsel can use in fraud litigation. * Partner with senior investigators and engineers to refine investigative methods, tooling, and report quality. **Qualifications** ------------------ * **Required:** Experience using AI coding agents, terminal coding agents, or CLI\-based AI development tools for research, writing, or code, with the judgment to validate their output (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, or open source tools). * Bachelor's or master's degree (or in progress) in cybercrime, cybersecurity, criminal justice, intelligence, computer science, or a related field. * 0\-2 years of experience in OSINT, investigations, threat intelligence, or a related discipline, including coursework, internships, CTF competitions, or military or government service. * Working knowledge of OSINT collection and analysis techniques and rigorous source documentation. **Preferred Qualifications** ---------------------------- * Experience integrating REST APIs and working with structured data (JSON), SQL for querying and analyzing large datasets. * Familiarity with graph and network analysis for detecting linked actor structures. * Understanding of detection\-performance concepts (precision, recall, false positives). * Familiarity with court records and legal documents, including dockets, deposition transcripts, and fraud complaints. * Proficiency in Python or a similar scripting language for data analysis and task automation. **Compensation \& Benefits** ---------------------------- * **Compensation:** The base salary range is $61,000 – $100,000, with flexibility depending on a candidate's background and experience. A company equity plan is also included in our compensation package. * **Well\-being:** 100% medical coverage with dental and vision. * **Sponsorship:** We welcome candidates on OPT (Optional Practical Training). We do not offer other visa sponsorship. * **Location:** This role is based on\-site 5 days per week in our Chelsea, NY office. * **Work Expectations:** This role requires a minimum of 50 hours per week. Thank you for your interest in Dashly Intelligence. Dashly Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact our Recruiting team. Compensation Range: $61K \- $100K

jobs.title: Full-Stack AI Engineer
jobs.description: **Full\-Stack AI Engineer — Liza** ================================== **About Liza** -------------- Liza Health is a Cambridge\-based startup building an AI\-enabled platform for modern primary care. Our bet is simple: primary care is the foundation of a healthy US health system, and AI finally makes it possible to rebuild and scale primary care from first principles instead of patching what's broken. Liza was co\-founded by Dr. Rushika Fernandopulle, a practicing physician who previously co\-founded Iora Health, the relationship\-based primary care company later acquired by One Medical and then Amazon, serial tech entrepreneur and investor Andy Palmer and healthcare serial entrepreneur Duncan Reece. We bring decades of experience redesigning care delivery together with a team that builds with frontier AI every day. We work alongside primary care practices to change how care is delivered: more time for relationships, less time on administrative burden, and patients who get the right care at the right time. If you want your engineering work to make care better for real patients and clinicians, this is the place. **The role** ------------ We're hiring AI Engineers who will design, build and ship the AI systems at the core of Liza's care model. You'll own problems end to end: sitting with clinicians and care teams to build real\-world healthcare applications for patients, clinicians and clinical operators. This is a generalist role by design. On any given week you might write a prompt and its eval suite, wire an agent into an EHR via FHIR, build a frontend feature for care coordinators, and develop healthcare data pipelines. We value curiosity, learning fast and shipping well. We don't care much about titles or hierarchy. The AI engineering bar here is the one set at the top AI labs: we A/B\-test agent changes in a harness, LLM judges score replies in production, and we review production traces every week. The difference is where the work lands: in the hands of patients and primary care teams across the US, helping real people live healthier lives while reducing overall healthcare costs. **What you'll do** ------------------ * Build production AI applications and agentic systems that support patients, clinicians and care teams across scheduling, intake, documentation, care coordination, outreach and clinical decision support. * Partner directly with patients, physicians, health coaches and operations staff to turn messy, real\-world workflows into clear technical requirements and measurable outcomes. * Work closely with our AI\-native design team to create experiences that are simple, efficient and effective for all of our users. * Design, test and iterate on prompts, context and tool definitions that shape how our models behave, and keep them versioned, reviewed and safe to change. * Define and run evaluations: build gold\-standard datasets with clinicians, write rubrics and automated graders, read transcripts for what the metrics miss, and set launch criteria before anything reaches a patient. * Integrate AI with our healthcare stack: our FHIR backend (Medplum), practice EHRs, HIE aggregators such as Metriport, HL7 interfaces, claims and scheduling systems, and our data platform. * Build with PHI, HIPAA, privacy, security and auditability in mind, including human\-review workflows and clear escalation paths for clinical risk. * Monitor systems in production and use error analysis, observability and user feedback to rapidly improve reliability, cost, latency and model selection. * Turn what we learn into reusable building blocks: shared eval harnesses, agent patterns, integration libraries and internal tools that make the whole team faster. **Who we're looking for** ------------------------- We want exceptional builders who believe in our mission and want to have a great time pursuing it. You'll fit right in if you are: * **A mission\-driven believer.** You think US healthcare can be dramatically better, that primary care is where that change starts, and that AI is the lever that makes it possible now. You want your work measured in better care, not just shipped features. * **A generalist.** You're comfortable across the stack and across problem types, from backend services and data pipelines to frontends, prompts and evals. You pick up new tools, domains and languages quickly, and you go wherever the problem is. * **An exceptional builder.** You take pride in shipping things people actually use at large scale and you have a track record of doing it. You move from idea to working prototype fast, then have the discipline to make it reliable. Startup experience is deeply appreciated at Liza. * **A strong teammate.** You do your best work on small, cross\-functional teams with clinicians, designers, operators and other engineers. You communicate clearly, share context generously, give and take direct feedback, and care more about the team winning than about who gets credit. * **Someone who has fun.** You bring c inevitable chaos of a startup, and building something meaningful with people you enjoy. * **Someone comfortable with ambiguity.** You can frame an unclear problem, make good calls with incomplete information, and own the outcome. No prior healthcare experience or clinical credentials are required. We'll teach you the domain; we're hiring for curiosity, judgment, craft and heart. **Essential AI skills** ----------------------- Strong candidates will be deep in several and conversant in all. * **Production LLM application engineering.** 5\+ years of software engineering (our stack is TypeScript end to end), with hands\-on experience shipping LLM\-powered products to real users at scale. * **Prompt and context engineering.** Designing, testing and optimizing system prompts, tool descriptions and retrieved context, and knowing each frontier model's strengths and failure modes; treating prompts as versioned, reviewed production code. * **Agents and tool use.** Building agentic workflows with function calling, multi\-step planning, memory and state management, and protocols like MCP, including multi\-agent systems with human oversight built in. * **Evaluation and error analysis.** Building datasets and rubrics with domain experts, LLM\-as\-a\-judge and automated graders, human rating workflows and regression detection, then reading transcripts, finding failure patterns and iterating until quality measurably improves. Evals are how we know a system is safe enough for patients. * **Retrieval and knowledge systems.** RAG pipelines, embeddings, structured knowledge and memory that let models reason reliably over large, messy, heterogeneous data such as longitudinal patient records. * **Full\-stack and systems breadth.** APIs, data infrastructure, web and mobile frontends, cloud deployment, CI/CD, containers and production observability. You can take a system from prototype to reliable production on your own. * **AI\-native development.** Fluency with coding agents and AI\-assisted workflows to multiply your own output. **Like to have** ---------------- * Experience with EHR and interoperability technologies such as Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, HL7, FHIR, SMART, health information exchanges and data aggregators such as Metriport, Zus, Gorilla Health, Redox. * Exposure to primary care, value\-based care, care coordination or patient access workflows. * Experience fine\-tuning or post\-training models, or building data programs for supervised fine\-tuning and reinforcement learning. * Voice or multimodal AI experience, such as patient\-facing phone agents or ambient documentation. * Prior work as a forward\-deployed engineer, technical founder or early engineer at a startup. * Open\-source contributions, publications or side projects that show your craft. **How we work and what we offer** --------------------------------- * **Small, cross\-functional teams.** Engineers, clinicians, designers and operators work side by side. Every person has real ownership and direct impact on patients. * **One codebase, shared by everyone**. Our APIs, web and mobile apps, infrastructure and agents live in one TypeScript monorepo, and every engineer ships across all of it, with coding agents as everyday tools. * **Speed with rigor.** We prototype fast, test with real users early, and hold a high bar for safety and quality before anything reaches care. * **Fun is part of the job.** We take the mission seriously, not ourselves. Expect team lunches, hack days, celebrating wins together, and colleagues you'll genuinely enjoy. * **Location:** Cambridge, MA, with in\-person collaboration. Hybrid encouraged \- most people are in the office 2\-3 days/week but we are flexible especially after ramp up. * **Compensation:** Competitive salary and meaningful equity, plus comprehensive health, dental and vision benefits. Liza is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, which make us better at building care for everyone.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description: **About Us:** Lovelace is the only provider of enterprise\-scale context engines capable of analyzing trillions of real\-time data points to create knowledge graphs that are usable by autonomous agents at the speed, scale, and accuracy required for mission\-critical analysis. Lovelace’s context engine platform, Elemental, uniquely integrates data ingestion, entity resolution, and graph building into a single pipeline that empower agentic deployments, delivering 1000X the investigative power for complex queries. With its proprietary ground\-breaking YottaGraph, Lovelace provides enterprises with real\-time, real\-world context, enabling agents to understand the impact of global intelligence on enterprise data for unmatched insights with millisecond precision. Founded in 2023 by Andrew Moore, former head of Google Cloud AI, dean of Carnegie Mellon’s School of Computer Science, and first AI advisor for U.S. CENTCOM, Lovelace currently works with some of the largest public and private enterprises in the world. **Job Summary:** * As a Machine Learning Engineer, you'll own ML problems end to end, from framing an ambiguous question to shipping a production system. There's no ticket queue and no narrow scope: everyone here, including newer engineers, stands up new jobs and makes changes across the codebase without close supervision. You'll decide what data matters, which models fit, and how the system around them should work. The role is roughly half research and half engineering, on a team that reports to our Chief Scientist. At Lovelace, every engineer is a manager of AI. Our engineers work alongside AI coding agents every day, and the most valuable thing you'll bring is judgment: knowing what to build, catching when an agent gets it wrong, and owning the design decisions. We're looking for people who ramp in weeks, not months. You don't need industry experience; strong research lab backgrounds are welcome. What matters is that you've owned hard problems and can think critically about your own work and your agents'. **Key Responsibilities:** * Frame ambiguous product needs as precise ML problems, and set your own requirements. * Decide what data is useful, which model types fit, and when to go beyond fine\-tuning. * Direct AI coding agents, review their output critically, and push back when their design decisions are wrong. * Design the systems around your models: data pipelines, serving, evaluation, and monitoring. * Choose metrics that reflect real outcomes, and catch when they mislead. * Stand up new jobs, make changes across the codebase, and ship NLP and LLM systems to production, owning their correctness. * Challenge assumptions, including teammates' and your own, to get to the right answer. **Qualifications:** * A track record of owning ambiguous problems end to end, in a research lab, a startup, or your own projects. * Strong ML fundamentals, from probabilistic foundations to modern deep learning and LLM architectures. * Experience building the system around a model, not just training it: data pipelines, evaluation, deployment, and how it behaves at scale. * Hands\-on experience with AI coding agents, and a clear sense of where they go wrong. * Expert\-level Python and a strong testing discipline. You understand how your code works. * The confidence to push back, with evidence, on requirements, teammates, and agents. **Preferred Skills:** * NLP, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, or agentic systems. * Go or other systems programming experience. * Open\-source contributions, side projects, or publications with working code. * Background from a strong research lab. A PhD is welcome but not required. **Benefits:** LovelaceAI offers competitive compensation packages, comprehensive benefits. We provide a supportive and inclusive work environment where your skills and expertise can make a significant impact on the safety and security of our communities. **Lovelace’s founding team includes:** **Andrew Moore**, who has a track record of building impactful AI systems, designing them with human rights impact assessments as a top priority, leading the AI division of one of the world’s foremost cloud companies, and actively participating in machine learning and AI research over the past two decades. **Toby Smith**, well known in the Pittsburgh Tech community for his engineering leadership and design skills, and who has led many of the most ambitious and complex system infrastructure projects in Google Pittsburgh and NetApp. Here is a note from Andrew Moore to people who are reading these Job Postings: “Hi folks, I’m so glad you are potentially interested in Lovelace AI. This area means a lot to me because while I am an AI optimist, I also think that we technologists owe it to a rightly skeptical world to show that modern intelligent systems can actually be useful. Usefulness comes in many guises: from life sciences to education and from transportation to entertainment and many others. For many of us, security and public safety is also very high on that list. That reasoning leads to this conclusion: I’m determined to make sure that the people building Lovelace AI gain a lot from the experience, including the chance to solve fascinating problems in computer science, AI, business development, customer success and product management. I also hope that we all learn from each other in a highly enriching work environment. But my main hope is that we have a shared sense of accomplishment as we see an increasing number of national security and public safety domains made safer through sensible and robust use of advanced computer science."

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer
jobs.description: Location: New Haven, CT, on\-site Full\-time Reports to: Chief Technology Officer Compensation: $200,000 \- $260,000/yearly plus bonus Company: Bexorg (Bexorg.com (https://bexorg.com)) **About Bexorg:** Bexorg is a precision neurology company working to transform how new medicines for central nervous system (CNS) diseases are discovered and developed. At the intersection of cutting\-edge neuroscience, AI, engineering, and translational drug development, our team combines scientific rigor, responsible stewardship, and cross\-disciplinary collaboration to advance innovative approaches to CNS therapeutics. Our flagship platform, **BrainEx**, is the world's first system to perfuse fresh, whole human postmortem brains through their intact vasculature, restoring and maintaining cellular biology, vascular reactivity, CSF circulation, and an intact blood\-brain barrier. This groundbreaking technology serves as the foundation of an active CNS therapeutics pipeline, including a Phase 1 program in Alzheimer's disease. Our second platform, **NeuroScale**, builds on this foundation by enabling high\-throughput, robotically handled brain\-slice experiments that extend research capabilities from hours to weeks. Every experiment conducted on these platforms carries significant scientific and ethical responsibility. The tissue is generously donated, each experiment is irreplaceable, and the resulting data must meet rigorous standards for accuracy, reliability, and regulatory scrutiny. The software that designs, records, and analyzes these experiments is therefore more than a supporting tool. It is an essential part of our technology, developed in\-house to ensure precision, accountability, and scientific integrity. To support this work, we are looking for curious, accountable individuals who are eager to take on meaningful challenges. At Bexorg, you will collaborate with colleagues who ask thoughtful questions, share ideas openly, and take ownership of moving complex work forward. Whether your expertise is in neuroscience, biology, engineering, data science, or operations, you will have the opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking research and help build a stronger foundation for the development of new CNS medicines. **The Role** We are seeking a **Principal Software Engineer** to own the software through which Bexorg's scientists design experiments on living human brain tissue and interrogate the data those experiments produce. You will lead two flagship efforts: our custom **LIMS**, which supports two applications, **Cortex** for BrainEx and **NeuroscaleOps** for NeuroScale; and **Neurolens**, our AI research harness, which you will re\-architect as a multi\-tenant platform for large pharma partners. This is a hands\-on principal role reporting to the CTO. You will set the technical direction, write a good share of the code, and ship to users who sit a few meters away. The first users of everything you build are the surgeons, perfusionists, neuroscientists, and drug discovery scientists who run the platforms. Their experiment designs become the data model, and the data model becomes the evidence behind our therapeutics. You will spend real time in the lab learning how an experiment on a human brain is actually designed: donors, protocols, dosing arms, sampling timepoints, regions, slices, plates, assays, readouts. You will turn that understanding into systems that make the right thing easy and mistakes hard, and that still make sense of the data years later. You will build on a strong foundation rather than a blank page: a multi\-account AWS estate, an S3\-based datalake, a LIMS in daily production use, and a working AI harness with 200\+ skills. The job is to take systems that already work for one company and make them precise enough for the FDA and general enough for our partners. **What You'll Build** * *1\. The LIMS: experiment design as the data model* Our custom **LIMS** supports two applications, **Cortex** for BrainEx and **NeuroscaleOps** for NeuroScale, on the backend data models beneath them. It is in daily production use. Its most pressing gap is also the most interesting software problem in the company: a first\-rate experience, and a first\-rate data model, for *designing* experiments. An experiment on a donated human brain is designed once and run once. Its design determines what every downstream dataset means: which regions are sampled, which compounds are dosed at which concentrations and timepoints, which slices go to which plates, wells, and assays. Captured as free text, the design leaves the datalake full of results nobody can fully interpret. Captured as validated structure, every readout arrives already knowing what it measures. You will build the loop that makes the second case the default: * Scientists describe our systems and protocols in natural language. * LLMs translate those descriptions into ontologies: the entities, relationships, and constraints of a BrainEx run or a NeuroScale slice ca r SOC 2\. * Real interest in drug discovery, and the patience to learn experiment design in depth from the scientists who do it. * Product sense: you notice when a tool is clumsy and fix it, and you can tell the difference between the feature scientists asked for and the one they need. * Fluency with LLM\-assisted engineering as a daily practice, paired with the judgment to know when the model is wrong. * Excellent written and verbal communication, and demonstrated experience mentoring engineers and setting technical standards. * Proven ability to operate as an aggressive self\-starter: you take ownership, move quickly, and drive projects forward with minimal supervision. * Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience with a strong track record of impact. * Based in, or willing to relocate to, the New Haven, CT area for an on\-site role. **Nice to Have** * Experience building or operating large multimodal omics datalakes: single\-cell or single\-nucleus transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, or high\-content imaging at scale, and the bioinformatics tooling around them (workflow engines such as Nextflow or Snakemake; scanpy, Seurat, or similar). * Experience with LIMS, ELN, or sample\-tracking systems, commercial (e.g., Benchling) or custom\-built, and strong opinions about why scientists dislike most of them. * Ontology engineering in the life sciences: OBO Foundry ontologies (UBERON, ChEBI, GO, Cell Ontology), knowledge graphs, or semantic\-web tooling. * Multi\-tenant SaaS architecture for enterprise or regulated customers, including security questionnaires, SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audits, and partner identity federation (SAML, OIDC). * Agentic AI infrastructure: tool and skill protocols, sandboxed execution, evaluation frameworks, and cost and latency control; experience with Amazon Bedrock or comparable model platforms. * Event\-sourced or bitemporal data architectures, and experience versioning schemas and data together. * Background in biopharma, preclinical research, or regulated environments (GLP, IND\-enabling studies, FDA submissions). * Hardware\-adjacent software: telemetry ingestion, IoT fleets (e.g., AWS IoT Greengrass), or lab automation and robotics integration. * Advanced degree (MS or PhD) in computer science, applied mathematics, computational biology, or a related field. **Why Bexorg** * Build software for a platform that exists nowhere else: perfused, metabolically active human brains and robotically handled human brain slices, producing data no other dataset on earth contains. * See the consequences of your work daily. The scientists using your experiment designer and your AI harness sit down the hall from the rigs, and the data they produce feeds an active CNS pipeline that includes a Phase 1 program in Alzheimer's disease. * Solve problems that matter beyond Bexorg. LLM\-derived ontologies as a validation layer, reproducible agentic research under regulatory scrutiny, and multi\-tenant AI infrastructure for pharma are open problems across the industry. You will solve them with real users and real stakes. * Own two systems at principal level, reporting directly to the CTO, in a fast\-moving, well\-funded TechBio company with active partnerships across major biopharma, leading academic institutions, government grantors, and the Michael J. Fox Foundation. * Work on\-site in New Haven, CT, with daily access to the lab, the rigs, the robots, and the people who run them. Compensation includes a competitive salary, meaningful equity, and benefits. This role is on\-site. The work depends on being beside the scientists and the systems they run, and we expect the person in this seat to be here. For a truly exceptional candidate, we are open to a conversation about location. If you want to build the software that lets an experiment on a human brain be designed once, run once, and trusted for years, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.description: Portland, Oregon, USA OR Austin, Texas, USA OR The Senior Firmware Design Engineer will spend 100% of working time performing the following duties: CPU Firmware Architecture and Development: Architect, develop, and maintain low\-level firmware and device drivers in C/C\+\+ and assembly language targeting bare\-metal and pre\-OS execution environments on RISC\-V processor platforms. Collaborate with security\-focused architecture teams to translate hardware security primitives into robust firmware\-enforced security policies. **Minimum Requirements**: * Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field, plus three (3\) years of post\-baccalaureate professional experience to include: * Developing low\-level device drivers and infrastructure firmware for SoC, CPU and/or GPU emulation platforms in C/C\+\+ programming language, targeting pre\-silicon execution environments. * ing practical knowledge of RISC\-based assembly code understanding and execution flow and verification purposes. * Performing hardware model bring\-up and debug activities using GDB\-based debug mechanisms and associated tooling. * Experience with memory\-mapped I/O peripheral configuration and DRAM initialization procedures. * Experience with industry\-standard software build systems (e.g. Make, CMake) and maintaining codebases using version control software (Git or Perforce). * Documenting infrastructure firmware design decisions and collaborating with hardware engineering and architecture teams to support software\-hardware integration. **What We Offer** * Competitive salary and benefits package. * Opportunities for professional growth in an innovative startup environment. * Collaboration with talented engineers passionate about cutting\-edge CPU technologies. * Opportunity to disrupt the CPU ecosystem

We're building the most AI\-native startup team in Los Angeles: operators, engineers and ML researchers building the transaction rails for the fast\-growing used EV market. **WHY PLUG** ------------ * You'll help build the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive. * You'll work on a platform built only for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive. * You'll be part of an AI\-native company that is rethinking how work gets done. * You'll work directly with operators who have scaled multi\-billion\-dollar businesses in automotive, EV and marketplaces. * You'll work alongside a small, senior team, with high autonomy and a direct line to company outcomes. **THE OPPORTUNITY** ------------------- Every car on Plug starts with a number: what is this EV worth today, and what will a dealer pay for it tomorrow? Those numbers come from our models. They draw on auction results, market data, vehicle telematics and battery health. As volume grows, our models have to get more accurate, update faster, and be easier to trust and explain. You'll join our Intelligence team and work alongside our ML engineer and data team, who built the models behind pricing and battery health. Together you'll take those models further: sharper price and volume forecasts, battery state\-of\-health models built from telematics, and LLM pipelines that pull structured data out of vehicle, title and inspection documents. **WHAT YOU'LL DO** ------------------ * Build and ship agents and multi\-agent workflows for operations, dealers, and sellers: document extraction, inspection and title review, dealer and seller communication, and internal tooling. * Trace every agent so you can see each step, tool call, and decision. Use those traces to debug failures and turn them into new eval cases. * Write evals before and alongside each agent: build datasets from real cases, measure accuracy and failure modes, and gate changes to prompts, models, and tools on the results. * Make model and prompt decisions with data: compare options on accuracy, cost, and latency, and run upgrades when a model is deprecated or a cheaper one holds up. * Integrate agents with the services the team already owns, through clean APIs and tools. Work within the existing architecture and raise design concerns with the owning engineer instead of routing around them. * Ship full\-stack when the job calls for it: the TypeScript and React screens where people review and correct agent output, and the backend endpoints behind them. * Help the rest of engineering adopt the same patterns. Build reusable tools, examples, and short write\-ups that make the next agent faster to build. **WHAT YOU'LL BRING** --------------------- * 5\+ years of full\-time industry software engineering, with a track record of shipping features to production and supporting them after launch. * Hands\-on experience shipping LLM features to production: tool use, retrieval, and structured output. * Experience building evals and tracing for LLM systems: datasets drawn from real cases, automated scoring, and production traces you used to find and fix failures. We care less about which agent framework you used (e.g., Claude Agent SDK, LangChain Deep Agents) than how you knew it worked. * Strong TypeScript or Python, and comfort working across the stack: APIs, databases, and frontend when needed. * You work agent\-first. You’ve built your own tooling around coding agents, such as skills, MCP servers, custom workflows, or evals. * You enjoy being part of a small team: pairing, reviewing each other’s work, sharing credit, and building inside systems other people designed. You can disagree, make your case, and then ship the agreed plan. * A habit of writing things down: short design notes, eval results, and runbooks that others can pick up. * High agency in an ambiguous, fast\-moving startup. You find the most valuable workflow to automate and ship against it without waiting for a perfect spec. * BS in computer science, math, statistics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent experience. **COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS** ----------------------------- **Annual salary:** $164,000 – $200,000 Salary ranges come from independent, third\-party benchmarking against national compensation data. Where an offer falls within the range depends on relevant experience, specialized skills, training and qualifications, current business needs and market conditions. We review ranges periodically and may adjust them as the market changes. ### **Benefits and perks** * Health, vision and dental insurance * 401(k) plan * 30 days of work from anywhere per calendar year * Daily lunch stipend * Equity (based on role and performance) * Unlimited PTO * Fully stocked kitchen * Dog\-friendly office * Ongoing opportunities for growth and development This is a full\-time, in\-person role based in our Los Angeles office in Sawtelle (between Santa Monica and West Los Angeles). We provide relocation assistance for candidates who need to move. Sponsorship is not available at this time. **Acknowledgments** Plug is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description: **Overview** **Role: Staff ML Engineer – experience in Semiconductor Domain.** **Location: San Jose, CA, USA. Day 1 onsite** **Department: ML** Job Description About the role We're looking for an ML engineer who works across the full stack from model to silicon — comfortable optimizing training and inference performance on GPU/AI\-accelerator infrastructure, building or tuning models, and adapting model and inference\-engine design to the constraints of the underlying chip and its NPU. You'll move fluidly between algorithm work, systems\-level software, and infrastructure work, closing the loop end\-to\-end rather than owning just one layer of the stack. What you'll do Optimize training and inference performance across GPU and AI\-accelerator infrastructure, including MLOps pipelines Design, train, and evaluate ML models (deep learning, LLM, CV, or recommendation systems) and take them into production Harden and extend NPU cores (e.g. building on an open RVV/tensor core like CoralNPU) into production silicon Build or optimize inference engines and serving runtimes against real hardware constraints — latency, memory, and power Work below the application layer where needed — BMC firmware, embedded Linux, or RTOS (e.g. Zephyr) — so AI features run reliably on real systems Build automated test/verification harnesses that close the loop for AI\-assisted RTL/DV, hardware bring\-up, or manufacturing test Apply ML to security — AI\-driven log/intrusion analysis, AI\-assisted penetration testing, or firmware/hardware security work Collaborate closely with RTL/hardware, firmware, and QA teams to ship AI features end\-to\-end, from training through deployment and monitoring Qualifications What we're looking for 5–7\+ years of hands\-on AI/ML experience; Master's required, PhD preferred Hands\-on experience with AI/ML infrastructure and performance — GPU clusters, distributed training, inference\-serving optimization, MLOps pipelines Model / algorithm development experience — designing, training, and evaluating ML models Experience taking models into production — feature engineering, data pipelines, deployment AI chip / hardware\-aware ML experience — optimizing inference engines for a specific chip, or adapting model architecture/quantization to chip constraints Deep, hands\-on expertise in at least 2 of the following 5 specialty areas — we don't expect all five: NPU / AI\-accelerator — hardening or extending an NPU core into production silicon, mapping models onto MAC/tensor\-engine constraints, or NPU\-aware RTL/DV work Systems / Sys\-level software — BMC firmware, embedded Linux, RTOS (e.g. Zephyr), or other low\-level system software Inference engine / runtime — built or materially optimized an inference engine or serving runtime against real hardware constraints Test / verification harness — built an automated harness that closes a loop, e.g. an agent\-driven RTL/DV test runner or a hardware bring\-up / MFG test harness Cyber security — AI\-driven log/intrusion analysis, AI\-assisted penetration testing, or firmware/hardware security Pay: $75\.00 \- $78\.00 per hour Expected hours: 40\.0 per week Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Thermal Engineer
jobs.description: **Build at the frontier, where superconductors, cryogenics, and megawatts meet** ================================================================================ Spinor Energy's mission is to accelerate the global transition to renewable energy with breakthrough technology. We’re building the real\-life flux capacitor: Superconducting Magnetic Energy Storage (SMES), a battery that stores electricity in the magnetic field of a superconducting coil instead of through chemical reactions. It never degrades, discharges megawatts in milliseconds, and is the most efficient form of energy storage ever conceived. Our engineering spans four disciplines at once: superconducting materials, megawatt\-scale power electronics, cryogenics, and vacuum systems. At Spinor, you'll get your hands on all of them. Spinor's founders came from SpaceX, where they designed Starlink solar arrays and scaled production to 70 satellites per week. We are bringing the same first\-principles engineering, rapid iteration, and design\-for\-scale mindset to energy storage. You will own consequential hardware architecture and first schematic through bring\-up, validation, and field deployment. **The Role** ============ We are hiring a Mechanical Engineer (Thermal / Cryogenics) to design and own Spinor’s cryogenic system, used to supercool superconducting magnets to temperatures colder than the surface of Pluto. **You Will** ============ * Own the design, analysis, and operation of Spinor’s cryogenic system from piece\-part design, to component selection, to guiding architectural decisions * Design and optimize the thermal budget and management of heat flux (conduction, radiation, convection) to the magnet * Own component design/selection and hardware delivery for key cryogenic and vacuum components: vacuum chambers/cryostats, multi\-layer insulation (MLI) radiation shielding, low\-conduction structural supports, and cryocooler interfaces * Own component selection, packaging, and operation of Spinor’s cryogenic auxillary equipment, including cryocoolers, helium compressors, water chillers, vacuum pumps, and water\-cooling loops, coordinating with facilities and customers to accelerate infrastructure development as needed * Oversee deployment of cryogenic assets in\-field operation and testing **Basic Qualifications** ======================== * Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Aerospace Engineering, another relevant discipline, or equivalent practical experience * Strong first\-principles fundamentals in mechanical design and design\-for\-manufacturing across a diverse set of manufacturing processes, including but not limited to injection molding, CNC/lathe, sheet metal, additive manufacturing, and forging/castings * Familiarity in applied GD\&T (ASME Y14\.5\), with experience designing and tolerancing complex assemblies for reliable fit\-up, preferably in a high\-rate, cost\-focused production environment * Strong proficiency with thermodynamic first principles across all forms of heat transfer, including but not limited to conduction, radiation, convection, and fluid dynamics **Preferred Qualifications** ============================ You have driven end\-to\-end product success across an entire hardware lifecycle, from initial problem statement through design, build\-out, and high\-rate manufacturing. You are not afraid to "Fail Fast" and can iterate quickly to de\-risk high\-impact requirements early in the development cycle You bring several of the following: * Experience in designing and simulation thermal and mechanical multi\-physics systems including CFD, (ANSYS or COMSOL preferred) * Experience in design, fabrication, and operation of cryocoolers, cryostats, vacuum chambers or pressure vessels * Hands\-on experience with the selection, packaging, integration, and operation of industrial cryogenic equipment, including cryocoolers, helium compressors, vacuum pumps, water chillers, and water\-cooling loops Relevant experience may include stored energy systems, aerospace thermal, battery pack design or manufacturing, or other technologies. We do not expect one person to have worked in every one of these areas. We care most about technical depth, learning velocity, and evidence that you can build and ship. Spinor Energy is an equal\-opportunity employer. Compensation Range: $125K \- $250K

jobs.title: Planning Engineer - Indiana
jobs.description: Are you ready to be part of a company that's not just talking about the future, but actively shaping it? Join The AES Corporation, the largest US\-based global power company with a team of 8,300 employees across 12 countries. AES has been **ranked \#1 by BloombergNEF** in renewable energy sales to corporations in the US and Americas for five consecutive years, providing electricity for **millions of people worldwide.** We are proud to foster a strong workplace culture, earning prominent positions in Great Place to Work™ rankings across the markets where we operate. AES was also named one of the World’s Most Ethical Companies for the 13th consecutive year in 2026, highlighting our dedication to integrity, transparency, and responsible business practices. Our spirit of innovation continues to earn industry recognition. AES is the only seven\-time winner of the Edison Electric Institute’s Edison Awards in the twenty\-first century, a distinction honoring global leadership in advancing the electric power industry. If you're ready to be part of a company that's not just adapting to change, but driving it, AES is the place for you. We're not just building a more sustainable future, we're powering it. Apply now and energize your career with a true leader in global energy. **We’re looking for a Planning Engineer to join our team in Indiana!** The Planning Engineer develops long\-term maintenance and capital investment project plans while providing technical support to thermal and renewable generation sites across the U.S. Under general supervision, this role is responsible for developing labor and material specifications, preparing project budgets, supporting material procurement, and reviewing bids for assigned projects. The Project Engineer is primarily responsible for labor and material specification development, budget development, material procurement, and bid review of assigned projects. Employee will be responsible for assisting as needed in the diagnosis of mechanical and electrical equipment issues, including technical direction to both contracted and plant personnel, as needed. Responsibilities: 1\) Perform any necessary inspections on mechanical/electrical generation equipment during outages or downtime as needed to support facility operations and project planning efforts. 2\) Create, scope, project justification, cost estimates, and budget future work plans for maintenance, upgrade, and replacement of assets. 3\) Reports and maintains current programs that assist the plant’s operations and maintenance division. 4\) Prepares estimates, construction drawings, material specifications and lists, procurement forms, work orders, contracts, and property record reports. 5\) Utilize Management of Change for controlling modifications to equipment, systems, and processes. 6\) Instructs and trains less senior or less experienced personnel on the technical aspects of their job, as assigned. 7\) Serves as a representative of the Company, as assigned. Ensure personal and contractor safety. 8\) Accepts short\-term assignments at other AES facilities. 9\) Ensure personal and contractor safety performance by meeting or exceeding AES safety policy requirements. 10\) Control project costs by completing economic evaluations for all applicable projects during budget process and for major emergent work, and maintaining project costs within allowed limits of approved cost estimate. 11\) Ensure Supply Chain engagement in procurement activities by providing bid specifications to Supply Chain in accordance with the procurement policy requirements. Provide generating station operations \& maintenance support by adequately responding to operational \& maintenance support requests in a timely and cooperative manner and actively participating in technical working groups as assigned. Is expected to accept temporary planning assignments at other AES facilities on an as needed basis. Qualifications: * Bachelor´s Degree or equivalent level of experience * Experience in Thermal and Renewable Electric Utility and Power Generation. * Strong computer skills to include Microsoft Suite required, SAP and GE APM experience helpful. * Strong background in Reliability Centered Maintenance Practices. * Maintenance and Reliability Professional Certification (CMRP) desirable. * Experience in project management with demonstrated ability to work in a team environment * Strong communicator, both oral and written. * Strong platform or public speaking skills for making presentations. * Demonstrated ability to work effectively and cooperatively with others as well as operate with a minimum of supervision. AES is an Equal Opportunity Employer who is committed to building strength and delivering long\-term sustainability through diversity and inclusion. Respecting all backgrounds, differences and perspectives enables us to improve the lives of our people, customers, suppliers, contractors, and the communities in which we live and work. In this role, you will: * **Lead through managers \-** you set direction, standards and priorities for a group of teams, and grow the managers who run them. * **Ship AI to production \-** you work with product to turn the AI roadmap into features firms use every day, with permissions, privacy and audit built in. * **Build shared platform capabilities \-** you make sure agents, APIs, search, data and workflow work reliably for every Actionstep product. * **Run AI responsibly and efficiently \-** you build evaluation, observability and cost discipline into how AI features are designed and run. * **Raise the bar on how we build \-** you bring every team in the group onto our AI development lifecycle and make delivery predictable. * **Lead across time zones \-** you run a group split between North America and Asia\-Pacific, which means some early or late calls. **Other Responsibilities:** * Undertaking any other reasonable duties as required **Requirements** **REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS** * **Director\-level leadership \-** you have led multiple teams through engineering managers. * **AI in production \-** you have shipped AI or agent features in a production SaaS product, including the evaluation, permissions, observability and cost management that come with them. * **Led AI PDLC adoption** \- you have moved an engineering org to AI\-driven development and can show what changed, with data.
